persona: c: Dr. Farhana Haque, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Health (senior non-technical decision-maker, national view, query ""). SIMULATED persona walkthrough run with an AI agent, not a real participant.

tasks.stuck: No 'this week' view. The map puts a triangle on almost every district (legend: 'cusum alert in range' = any alert in 26 weeks), so the map cannot answer 'who is on alert now'. The ranking table orders by 'Alert wks' over 07 Jul-29 Dec 25, not by current status; 'Peak ÷ thr', 'Mean /100k', '80% PI' unexplained, and header hover gives no tooltip. Picked Dhaka (row 1, dengue) but could not tell whether Dhaka is on alert this week or was months ago (its chart shows the peak in Oct/Nov and near-zero cases by late Dec). Table shows 'Latest wk 160' while the chart's y-axis shows up to 150k cases/week for Dhaka; the two numbers do not look like the same thing. Only by clicking each disease button separately could she see other diseases; there is no all-disease summary. Some rows show 'Latest wk <5' but 'Next wk forecast 183' (diarrhoea, Lalmonirhat), which looks wrong to her.
quotes: Nearly the whole map has orange triangles. If everything is an alert, what am I supposed to act on?
I asked which districts are on alert this week. This table tells me how many weeks they were on alert since July. Those are different questions.

tasks.stuck: Next week is only in the table: '953, 80% PI 604-1,340'. She can guess 953 is the expected number but not that '80% PI' means 'probably between 604 and 1,340'. No four-week figure is shown anywhere as text; on the chart the forecast is a thin dashed line squashed against zero because the axis is scaled to the 150k peak. The hover readout over the chart gives 'Threshold (ears_c2): 3.0' next to 'Observed: 52,690' and 'cusum: stat 4.89 / thr 5.00', which is meaningless to her. 953 next week vs 160 latest week is a 6x jump with no explanation.

What is 'PI'? What is 'q10-q90'? Just tell me: most likely this many, could be up to that many.

quotes: If a journalist asks me why Dhaka got more, the honest answer from this screen is: I don't know. Dhaka already has twelve times what it needs.

issues.problem: Triangle marks any alert in the 26-week range, so nearly every district has one; cannot see who is on alert now. 'cusum' unexplained.

issues.problem: No national summary: how many districts on alert this week, for which diseases. Must click each disease button separately.
